## Who was Arthur Schopenhauer?

Arthur Schopenhauer (1788–1860) was a German philosopher of pessimism whose The World as Will and Representation fused Kantian phenomena with a blind metaphysical will. Largely ignored while Hegel dominated Berlin, he later won fame influencing artists and psychologists. He drew on Platonic Ideas and—among the first Europeans so deeply—Indian thought. Handbook dates: 1788–1860. Aphorisms on life’s suffering made him a literary philosopher.

## Major ideas

The world is representation structured by space, time, and causality; underlying it is will—endless striving without final satisfaction. Aesthetic contemplation briefly quiets will, especially in music. Compassion is the basis of ethics; egoism expresses will’s conflict. Ascetic denial of the will-to-live is salvation’s path. Character is innate; motivation can be explained but not casually remade. Eastern renunciation motifs corroborate his pessimism.

## Major works

-   The World as Will and Representation
-   On the Fourfold Root of the Principle of Sufficient Reason
-   Parerga and Paralipomena
-   On the Basis of Morality

[Every work in this archive →](https://www.philosophydef.com/works)

## Legacy

Schopenhauer shaped Wagner, Nietzsche’s early thought, Freud’s climate, and modernist literature. Pessimism and aesthetics curricula still assign him. He opened European philosophy toward Buddhism and the Upanishads.

Original language & citation

## Reading and citing Arthur Schopenhauer responsibly

Original languages on record

German

Language of the works

German

How to cite

Name the volume as well as the work, and give the section number for Vol. 1 and the chapter for Vol. 2 — the two volumes are organised differently. The Aphorisms are a part of Parerga, not a separate book.
